headline: High: Dify can write and execute server-side code while Plane accepts uploaded files and broad egress, creating default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can ingest uploaded knowledge-base files and run tools in agent/workflow flows, while Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from Plane can reach Dify as trusted input. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Plane-uploaded content is copied into Dify knowledge-base files or prompts, injection is possible.
IF Dify treats uploaded file text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Restrict cross-system copy-paste of file contents.
Add a manual review step before importing Plane artifacts into Dify.
Prefix imported content with provenance labels.
Disable tool execution for untrusted imports.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, model-provider keys, and tool credentials. Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps. If the same workspace data is shared, either side can expose sensitive material through outbound requests or uploads. The shared-data path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF the same files or notes are imported into both systems, leakage risk exists.
IF Dify tools send imported content to external model providers, shared data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive Plane data out of Dify imports.
Review Dify tool and model-provider destinations.
Use separate credentials for each system.
Limit uploaded files to non-sensitive samples.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Plane cannot write the filesystem, but it does accept file uploads and broad egress. The main conflict is not direct write-write collision, but Dify's server-side writes can race with shared artifacts if both are pointed at the same workspace or datastore. Because shared-state details are only partially documented, uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both systems target the same shared directory or datastore, concurrent mutation can collide.
IF Dify workflows write artifacts derived from Plane uploads, stale overwrites can occur.
mitigations: Separate the two systems' working directories.
Avoid shared mutable mounts.
Schedule writes so only one system mutates a given artifact.
Check for file-lock support before enabling shared storage.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can produce agent/workflow outputs and execute tools; Plane can consume files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks. If Plane content is fed into Dify and then rendered or acted on without verification, errors can cascade from one system to the other. The pathway exists in default-style integrations, but there is no direct evidence of automatic trust, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plane content is used as Dify input without validation, hallucinations or bad facts can propagate.
IF Dify tool outputs are copied into Plane tasks or issues, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before copying outputs between systems.
Mark Dify outputs as untrusted until checked.
Use templates that separate facts from recommendations.
Log source provenance on imported items.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between Dify and Plane.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Dify handles conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while Plane handles issues, tasks, files, and notes, so compliance concerns are possible only if the operator places regulated data into both. Because the profiles do not show a concrete mismatch, this stays low and cites both profiles for the touched data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in both systems under different retention policies, compliance drift can occur.
IF either deployment is bound to a residency or certification requirement not shown here, a mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in both systems.
Document retention settings for each deployment.
Confirm residency and certification claims before production use.
Separate compliance-sensitive projects from general work.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across deployments.
